entries.title: Non-thin rank jumps remain outside the entire smooth rational bisection atlas, including all generic translations
entries.scope: New written corollary of the completed quotient, index theorem and verified Pasten--Salgado application. Every smooth rational original-degree2 curve is an arithmetic-genus0 minus2 curve, so its orbit belongs to the complete40917 norm10 classes. All are Q-parametrizable; generic translations preserve the original base parameter. Hence their entire rational incidence set S2 is the union of40917 fixed degree2 P1-to-P1 images, is thin, and has O(B) rational parameters of original height at most B. The latter follows from degree2 height growth; no effective constant or complete equation enumeration is supplied. Since the parent's smooth rank-at-least18 parameter set R18 is non-thin, R18 minus S2 remains non-thin. Even an exhaustive smooth rational bisection atlas cannot explain all rank jumps. This does not locate302 in or outside S2, prove positive density, exclude singular rational curves of positive arithmetic genus or positive-genus covers, or restrict general pointed-quartic searches to the minus2 atlas. The implication is written, not a new independent replay of its census or analytic dependencies; no computation or search is required.

entries.title: Marked finite-level rootless reachability
entries.scope: Let V be a positive-definite rational quadratic space of dimension greater than two, let Lambda be an integral lattice, and encode a finite discriminant/glue marking by a compact-open level subgroup K^lev of O_V(A_f), with all nonunimodular and marking primes in a finite bad set S. Let X(K^lev) be the finite marked class set, s:X(K^lev)->S(K^lev) its spinor-genus map, and S_1(K^lev) the subgroup of good-prime spinor displacements. Suppose the marking functorially determines a graph-glue completion W_x and its physical reverse-mask witnesses. Then a state x reaches a rootless completion by finitely many witness-killing good-prime core-neighbor edges if and only if a rootless state z exists with s(z)=s(x) modulo S_1(K^lev). In fact, for every sufficiently large good prime p with delta_p=s(z)s(x)^(-1), Chenevier's level-structure equidistribution theorem gives a one-step p-neighbor marked-isomorphic to z. Such a rootless child automatically kills every parent physical witness by the zero-layer survival law and has no replacement birth. The compatible primes form nonempty arithmetic progressions; finiteness of the marked class set gives a finite non-effective sufficient prime set for each component, with at most one prime per required element of S_1(K^lev). Thus fixed-prime traps may persist, but no all-good-prime directed trap exists inside a finite marked component containing a rootless state. No effective prime threshold, infinite-vector marking, core-to-elliptic-neighbor lift, equation, or J1 classification is supplied.
dependencies: external: Chenevier, Statistics for Kneser p-neighbors, Theorem 5.9 and Remarks 5.10--5.11

entries.title: Specialization quotient, rank-jump sandwich, and midpoint/class-group structure
entries.scope: Let E_eta/K(T) have certified full generic free Mordell--Weil group M_eta of rank r, let E_t/K be a smooth specialization whose image M has rank r, and let M be contained in a certified subgroup L of E_t(K). For every prime ell, the free quotient gain and residual Selmer dimension give rank(L/M) <= rank E_t(K)-r <= dim_Fell(Sel_ell(E_t/K)/bar(M)_ell); without preservation of rank r the left term is only a quotient gain. The canonical-height quotient by M is the orthogonal-complement norm hhat_/M(P)=inf_{u in M tensor R} hhat(P+u), computed by the Schur complement and distinct from an integral coset minimum. For Q in M, orthogonal projection gives hhat(2R-Q)/4=hhat_/M(R mod M)+hhat(pr_M(R)-Q/2), and the paired heights add hhat(R)+hhat(Q-R)=hhat(Q)/2+2hhat_/M(R mod M)+2hhat(pr_M(R)-Q/2). If mu_2(c) is the minimum height in c in M/2M, then the midpoint depth is mu_2(c)/4, the two-torsion-restricted covering radius is max_c sqrt(mu_2(c))/2, and this is a lower bound for the full covering radius. Finally, everywhere-even squareclasses have the ideal square-root map c:ker(v)->Cl(F)[2]. For positive-square-norm subspaces G contained in B supported on S, dim c(ker(v_S|B))/c(ker(v_S|G)) is at least dim(B/G)-(rank v_S(B)-rank v_S(G))-u_F^+; in odd degree u_F^+=r1+r2-1. This last result is a known-point-forced full-class-group image lower bound, not an S-class-group computation, Selmer upper bound, or prospective rank predictor. The theorem package makes no exact specialized-rank or bounded-search claim beyond its stated certified inputs.

entries.title: Global residual Selmer subspaces, Cassels-Tate radical, and covering complexity
entries.scope: For A=E(K), a finitely generated subgroup M of rank r, G=delta(M), and epsilon=dim_F2((A/M)[2]), the Kummer sequence gives W_G=A/(M+2A), an exact sequence 0->W_G->Sel_2/G->Sha[2]->0, and dim W_G=rank(A)-r+epsilon. The residual Cassels-Tate radical modulo W_G is exactly 2 Sha[4], so neither isotropy nor the radical certifies rational solubility. A complete residual pairing of dimension s and rank 2a gives rank(A)<=r+s-2a-epsilon; a partial restricted matrix does not give a full rank bound. For a point P=(a,b) on a short model, the pointed quartic w^2=t^4-6at^2-8bt-3a^2-4A with its explicit birational map phi_P becomes the actual cover delta(P) only with the degree-four map 2phi_P-P. The cubic norm equations give an explicit two-quadric model with rational witness. A generic midpoint centre Q in M has residual cover class zero even though its birational chart discovers points in every W_G class; paired points R and Q-R have the same residual label. Model-and-map encoding cost together with witness cost defines an increasing soluble-class span filtration exhausting W_G, with an exact rank implication and a constructive point-height-to-quartic-coefficient bound. These are standard descent consequences and explicit deductions, not a proof of a prospective jump predictor.
